The checker rejected the program because the word "input" appeared in two comments. I removed it and also cleaned up the redundant Q expressions. The circuit and sizing are unchanged.

A rough first-order check suggests the design meets every spec, but it has not been simulated yet:

| Spec | Requirement | Estimate | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transimpedance gain | ≥ 112 dBΩ | about 113 dBΩ | Rf = 450 kΩ, provided loop gain is high |
| Noise at 1 MHz | ≤ 250 fA/√Hz | about 195 fA/√Hz | Mostly Rf thermal noise |
| Power | ≤ 47 µW | 36 µW | 1.8 V × (10 µA + 10 µA) |
| Bandwidth | ≥ 23 MHz | depends on M1 | gm1 / C at the amplifier node must give (1+T)·ωa·ωi ≈ (2π·23 MHz)² |

The bandwidth is the spec most likely to be at risk.

```python
PARAMS = {
    "gmid1": (15.0, 8.0, 22.0),     # front CS device gm/Id
    "L1":    (0.3, 0.15, 1.0),      # front CS length (sets A1 / amp pole)
    "gmidf": (17.0, 8.0, 22.0),     # follower gm/Id
    "Lf":    (0.15, 0.15, 0.5),     # follower length
    "If":    (10e-6, 4e-6, 14e-6),  # follower bias current
    "Rf":    (450e3, 410e3, 700e3), # feedback resistor
    "Cf":    (0.3e-15, 0.1e-15, 20e-15),  # feedback cap (peaking control)
}

def design(p, lut, spec):
    cpd = spec.get("cpd", 5e-13)
    cl = spec.get("cl", 2e-13)
    iref = spec.get("iref", 10e-6)
    VDD = 1.8
    Rf, Cf, If = p["Rf"], p["Cf"], p["If"]

    # M1: CS gain device; its drain current is IREF itself, delivered into node "ibias" (amp node a)
    m1 = lut.size("n", p["gmid1"], p["L1"], iref, vds=1.1)
    vg_dc = m1.vgs                  # no DC current in Rf -> vout_dc = Vgs1
    vout_dc = vg_dc

    # Follower: drain at VDD, source at vout, resistor sink to vss
    mf = lut.size("n", p["gmidf"], p["Lf"], If, vds=VDD - vout_dc, vsb=vout_dc)
    Rl = vout_dc / If
    va_dc = vout_dc + mf.vgs        # node a DC (M1 vds)

    n = Netlist("iin vout vdd vss ibias")
    n.dev("M1", "ibias", "iin", "vss", "vss", m1)
    n.dev("MF", "vdd", "ibias", "vout", "vss", mf)
    n.R("RL", "vout", "vss", Rl)
    n.R("RF", "vout", "iin", Rf)
    n.C("CF", "vout", "iin", Cf)

    # ---------- analytic predictions ----------
    gl = 1.0 / Rl + 1.0 / Rf
    avf = mf.gm / (mf.gm + mf.gmbs + mf.gds + gl)    # follower gain
    A1 = m1.gm / m1.gds                              # ideal IREF load
    T = A1 * avf                                     # loop gain
    zt = Rf * T / (1.0 + T)

    Ca = m1.cdd + m1.cgd + mf.cgd + mf.cgg * (1 - avf) * 0.7 + 2e-15
    Cin = cpd + m1.cgg + 2e-15
    Cfe = Cf + m1.cgd                                # Miller cap adds to feedback cap
    wa = m1.gds / Ca
    wi = 1.0 / (Rf * (Cin + Cfe))
    wf = (mf.gm + mf.gmbs + gl) / (cl + mf.cgg * 0.3 + 5e-15)

    wn = math.sqrt((1 + T) * wa * wi)
    Q = wn / (wa + wi + (1 + T) * wa * wi * Rf * Cfe)
    Q = max(Q, 0.3)
    k = 1 - 1 / (2 * Q * Q)
    f3 = wn * math.sqrt(k + math.sqrt(k * k + 1)) / (2 * PI)
    # degradation from the follower pole (third pole)
    f3 = f3 / math.sqrt(1 + (2 * PI * f3 / wf) ** 2) ** 0.5

    kT4 = 4 * 1.380649e-23 * 300.15
    en2 = kT4 * 0.8 / m1.gm
    w1m = 2 * PI * 1e6
    in2 = kT4 / Rf + en2 * (w1m * (Cin + Cfe)) ** 2 + en2 / Rf ** 2
    in_noise = math.sqrt(in2) * 1.1                  # 10% allowance for flicker noise

    power = VDD * (iref + If)

    return n, {
        "zt_dbohm": db(zt),
        "f3db": f3,
        "in_noise_1m": in_noise,
        "power": power,
        "vout_dc": vout_dc,
        "va_dc": va_dc,
        "loop_gain": T,
        "Q": Q,
    }
```
